support_alex: Escalation from a customer (ACME) — they see intermittent 'invalid JSON' errors when using JSON mode + streaming responses. Happens only when the client enables gzip on the request and when their OAuth token refresh occurs mid-stream. They provided a small Go repro and server logs.

devon: Can you paste the exact error the customer sees and the Go snippet?

support_alex: Error from their app: `json: unexpected EOF` from json.Decoder.Decode while parsing the streaming payload. They also see truncated frames in our nginx access logs. Here is the customer's minimal repro (they say it fails ~1/20 runs):

```go
// simplified repro (Go 1.20)
req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses?mode=json", bytes.NewReader(promptBytes))
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer <short-lived-token>")
req.Header.Set("Accept-Encoding", "gzip") // they enable gzip
resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
defer resp.Body.Close()
reader, _ := gzip.NewReader(resp.Body)
dec := json.NewDecoder(reader)
for {
 var msg map[string]interface{}
 if err := dec.Decode(&msg); err == io.EOF { break }
 if err != nil { log.Println("decode error:", err); break }
 fmt.Println("got", msg)
}
```

sarah: Hmm — they are decompressing client-side which is ok. But streaming + gzip + chunked transfer can interact badly if gzip is applied after chunking incorrectly. Do we know whether our proxy/runtime sets `Content-Encoding: gzip` or if the client is requesting gzip?

mike: From runtime logs we see the request has `Accept-Encoding: gzip`. Our gateway sets `Content-Encoding: gzip` for responses when compression is enabled. But for streaming responses we should be using `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and stream compressed chunks. There is a known risk: if the upstream does server-side gzip but we also do any buffering or token refresh that closes/reopens the backend connection, some intermediate proxies might re-chunk differently and corrode gzip frames, producing truncated gzip stream.

support_alex: The customer says the token was being refreshed by their SDK mid-stream which caused a 401 from our infra and then an automatic retry that resumed the stream. They think the retry path re-encoded/resumed the gzip stream incorrectly.

devon: Do we have the nginx/gateway access & error logs around the time? Any 401s or 502/503?

support_alex: Pasted snippets from the customer's request trace and our gateway:

```
gateway.log 2026-11-07T14:12:45Z INFO upstream_conn reset during write (client auth refresh)
gateway.log 2026-11-07T14:12:45Z WARN started retry to backend id=arn:... cause=401
gateway.log 2026-11-07T14:12:46Z INFO backend response started headers: Transfer-Encoding: chunked, Content-Encoding: gzip
gateway.log 2026-11-07T14:12:46Z INFO backend resumed stream with new backend connection, resumed bytes: 0x... (gzip frame boundary may be lost)
```

sarah: That matches a classic case where an interrupted gzip stream gets resumed from a different connection and the concatenated chunks don't form a valid gzip member stream for the decoder. Some decoders tolerate concatenated gzip members, others (Go's gzip.Reader) expect a proper gzip stream. The json.Decoder then sees an EOF mid-object and returns `unexpected EOF`.

mike: Short-term workaround: tell customers to disable response compression (`Accept-Encoding: identity`) for streaming JSON mode or to have the SDK handle `Content-Encoding: gzip` by reassembling and validating gzip members. Long-term: we should avoid applying gzip at the gateway for streaming JSON responses — instead use per-chunk compression or advertise `Content-Encoding: identity` and let clients compress on demand.

devon: Can SDK team add a guard to the Go/TS/Python SDKs to skip `Accept-Encoding: gzip` for `mode=json` streaming endpoints and log a clear warning? That would be a low-risk mitigation.

sarah: I'll open a PR for the Go SDK to explicitly set `Accept-Encoding: identity` when `stream=true && mode=json` and add a note in the docs. Also add an integration test that simulates mid-stream token refresh to ensure no silent truncation.

mike: From infra side I'll add a config flag to the gateway to avoid gzip for streaming responses (opt-out for non-streaming compressed responses). We'll also add an instrumented metric for "stream-resume-count" to detect how often we reattach streams.

support_alex: Customer-facing suggested message: "We recommend disabling Accept-Encoding: gzip for streaming JSON mode. We're shipping SDK fixes and a gateway change to make this automatic; ETA 3 business days. In the meantime, you can set Accept-Encoding: identity to avoid the issue." :thumbsup:

sarah: noting action items — PR -> Go SDK + docs, add test, coordinate with infra for gateway opt-out.

mike: I'll prioritize gateway flag, will post config patch and rollout plan here when ready.

support_alex: thanks all — i'll send the suggested mitigation to the customer and escalate for the dedicated account. :white_check_mark:
